memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "The Lord said to Moses and Aaron, "When Pharaoh says to you, 'Perform a miracle,' then say to Aaron, 'Take your staff and throw it down before Pharaoh,' and it will become a snake."" - Exodus 7:8-9 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Look at how carefully God prepares them. When Pharaoh says this, you do that. God anticipates the exact demand and gives them the answer in advance.

Moses would walk into that throne room already knowing what would be asked of him. That is a great mercy. He did not have to improvise before the most intimidating man in the world.

God often does this for us, though we notice it only afterwards. The verse we read that morning turns out to be exactly what we needed by evening. The conversation we had last month prepared us for the crisis this week. Our God goes ahead of His people.

There is also significance in the sign itself. The cobra was a symbol of Pharaoh's royal power, worn on his crown. God chose to display His authority using the very image Egypt trusted in. He would meet Pharaoh on his own ground.

Whatever room you must walk into today, God has been there first.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Where can I see, looking back, that God prepared me before I knew I needed it?
2. What conversation am I dreading that I can entrust to Him now?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, thank You that You go ahead of me. Prepare me for what today holds and give me the words I will need. Amen.
